groups.A: Known rule, new wording (VM Import, Budgets, Service Catalog, DR tier, WAF + usage plan)
groups.B: Multi-select half right (one correct pick, one plausible distractor kept)
groups.C: Access & security design (no open ports, multi-AZ + WAF logging, cross-account write)
groups.D: Service fit / hidden constraint (Lambda vs Fargate, Snowball tuning, DX carriers, licensing, PHZ association)

1.keywords: redirect 10 domains by JSON route, HTTP and HTTPS, least operational effort, select three
1.trap: Picked C and D: a plain Lambda or API Gateway needs code change per JSON update and misses the edge. Missed ALB HTTP/HTTPS listeners (B) and ACM SAN certificate (F).
1.rule: Many domains: ACM cert with SANs + CloudFront Lambda@Edge for redirect logic; ALB needs both HTTP and HTTPS listeners.

4.keywords: 15 GB/day statistics, S3 plus Athena, date-range queries, optimal performance, select two
4.trap: Picked B: a bucket per date range is not an Athena tuning practice. Missed Hive-style date partitioning (E), which prunes scans for date queries.
4.rule: Athena speed: columnar Parquet/ORC + date partitions so date-range queries scan less data.

5.keywords: bastion SSH replacement, auditing, increase security control, Amazon Linux 2, VPN
5.trap: Picked EC2 Instance Connect: it needs inbound port 22 reachable and gives weaker audit than Session Manager. Session Manager uses IAM role, no inbound ports, logged sessions.
5.rule: Auditable access without open ports or bastions: SSM role + Session Manager; remove port 22 rules.

11.keywords: on-premises VMware app to EC2, preserve software and configuration
11.trap: 🔁 Picked DataSync + FSx for Windows datastore: wrong tool, VMware data store is not a file share. Intended path is OVF export to S3 then VM Import.
11.rule: VM as-is to EC2: export OVF/OVA to S3, VM Import role, import-image.

13.keywords: Redshift cost per team, budget threshold notification, view spend, multi-account, select two
13.trap: 🔁 Picked C (CloudTrail data events plus billing alarm): CloudTrail logs API calls, not cost. Missed Budgets resource in CloudFormation (A) plus Service Catalog products (E).
13.rule: Cost alerts = AWS Budgets, not CloudTrail or CloudWatch agent; self-service enforced centrally = Service Catalog products with budgets attached.

15.keywords: batch scripts to serverless microservices, steps take seconds, most cost-effective, orchestrate
15.trap: Picked Fargate containers + Step Functions: serverless but costlier than Lambda for seconds-long steps. Lambda fits under the 15-minute limit; Step Functions orchestrates.
15.rule: Short steps + serverless + orchestration: Lambda + Step Functions; Fargate costs more, EventBridge is not an orchestrator.

16.keywords: AD domain controllers as DHCP DNS, interface endpoint names not resolving, select two
16.trap: Picked E (VPC resolver as secondary DNS): a secondary DNS is only a failover, not split by query. Fix is DC forwarding of non-authoritative queries (D).
16.rule: Custom DNS servers need a forward path to the VPC resolver; secondary DNS does not split queries.

17.keywords: highly available EC2 app, filter common vulnerabilities, send rejected requests to third-party audit
17.trap: Picked B: ALB with instances but no multi-AZ Auto Scaling group, and WAF logs via CloudWatch plus Lambda polling. Needs multi-AZ ASG, managed rules, WAF logging to Firehose.
17.rule: HA = multi-AZ Auto Scaling group; WAF logs go to Kinesis Data Firehose, which can deliver to third-party endpoints.

22.keywords: expense app Friday bursts, finance month-end reports, HA, least operational overhead, select two
22.trap: Picked B (ECS behind ALB): containers still need cluster or capacity management unless Fargate. Serverless S3/CloudFront + API Gateway + Lambda (C) has least overhead.
22.rule: Least overhead + bursty: serverless front/back end (S3, CloudFront, API Gateway, Lambda); S3 + Athena + QuickSight for reports.

27.keywords: Route 53 API throttling from Lambda at thousands of Spot instances, buffering, select three
27.trap: Picked A (SQS FIFO): FIFO is not required here, ordering is irrelevant; a standard queue buffers the events. Rule intended is standard SQS as the target (E).
27.rule: Route 53 API rate limit: buffer events in SQS (standard is enough), batch API calls from Lambda.

32.keywords: Reserved Instances should cover 70% of workload, alert DevOps if coverage drops
32.trap: 🔁 Picked Cost Explorer RI utilization report: utilization is purchased RI hours used, not coverage, and Cost Explorer does not alert. Use a Budgets RI coverage budget.
32.rule: RI coverage threshold alert = AWS Budgets coverage budget; utilization is a different metric.

34.keywords: three-tier app, two Regions, failover within 1 minute, NoSQL tier, select three
34.trap: 🔁 Picked F (active/active on Spot): Spot capacity can be reclaimed, unacceptable for the always-on production tier. Pick active/passive ASG with zonal RIs plus On-Demand (E).
34.rule: Always-on production tier: Reserved baseline + On-Demand, never Spot; DR tier matches 1-minute RTO with failover record and low TTL.

37.keywords: CloudHSM M of N quorum authentication first-time setup, two of four officers, select two
37.trap: Picked D (IAM policy): the quorum value is set inside the HSM by a CO, not in IAM. Missed registering the signing key with registerMofnPubKey (A).
37.rule: CloudHSM quorum setup: CO registers signing keys, then sets M value in the HSM; token comes after setup.

41.keywords: API Gateway Regional REST API, botnet traffic, few US companies twice daily, secure at minimum cost
41.trap: 🔁 Picked CloudFront + WAF per-day rate rule: WAF rate rules use short windows, not per day; CloudFront adds cost. Needs WAF IP allow-list plus usage plan and API key.
41.rule: Known client IPs + low volume: WAF IP allow-list on the API, usage plan + API key; skip CloudFront.

44.keywords: SAML 2.0 federation fails for test users, what to check, select three
44.trap: Picked C (users' permission policy for AssumeRoleWithSAML): federated users are not IAM users; trust and mapping matter. Missed IdP assertions mapping users to roles (F).
44.rule: SAML federation checks: role trust policy names SAML provider, IdP assertion maps to roles, portal calls AssumeRoleWithSAML.

53.keywords: Windows and Linux EC2, RDP/SSH open to world, most secure management, no corporate connection
53.trap: Picked VPN with RDP/SSH open from corporate range: ports still open and weaker auditing. Session Manager needs no inbound ports and logs sessions.
53.rule: Most secure instance admin: Session Manager with IAM permissions; no inbound RDP/SSH, no bastion.

55.keywords: 50 TB millions of small files, Snowball Edge copy slow, encryption overhead
55.trap: Picked USB direct copy: Snowball Edge has no USB data interface. Intended speedup is parallel copy operations from separate Snowball client instances.
55.rule: Snowball small-file speed: run multiple parallel copy commands, batch small files, copy directories.

56.keywords: single Direct Connect private VIF, business-critical, most resilient connectivity
56.trap: Picked VPN to separate VGWs: internet VPN is a less reliable backup than a second DX. Second DX from a different carrier gives physical diversity; VGW is already redundant.
56.rule: Most resilient hybrid link: second Direct Connect from a different carrier/location; VPN is a cheaper backup only.

70.keywords: Dev account pipeline upload to Prod S3 bucket, OAI-only policy, uploads denied
70.trap: Picked bucket-owner-full-control ACL: the bucket policy allows only the OAI, so Dev role is denied before any ACL applies. Needs a Prod-account role to write.
70.rule: Cross-account S3 write when bucket only trusts OAI: assume a role in the bucket account.

72.keywords: Oracle on EC2, eliminate licensing costs, scalability and reliability, unstructured data
72.trap: Picked RDS Oracle Multi-AZ: still licensed Oracle, so licensing cost is not eliminated. Unstructured data moves to DynamoDB.
72.rule: Eliminate Oracle licensing: move to open-source engine or DynamoDB; RDS Oracle keeps license cost.

74.keywords: hybrid DNS, private hosted zone, on-premises and all VPCs resolve internal.company.local, highest performance
74.trap: Picked D: PHZ associated only to the shared services VPC, so other VPCs cannot resolve. Associate the PHZ with all VPCs and use inbound endpoint.
74.rule: On-premises to PHZ = inbound resolver endpoint; PHZ must be associated with every VPC that should resolve it.
